seoDescription: Learn how to automatically generate interactive Swagger API documentation for your Golang applications using the Swaggo library. This step-by-step guide demonstrates integrating Swaggo with a Fiber web framework project. You'll see how to use Go annotations to define API endpoints, parameters (path, header, body), request/response models, and status codes. Discover how to initialize the Swaggo CLI, generate swagger.json and swagger.yaml files, and serve a rich, browsable UI for your API.

chapters.title: Introduction to Swagger and Swaggo
chapters.description: This chapter provides a brief overview of what Swagger is and introduces the Swaggo library for generating API documentation from Go annotations.

chapters.title: Overview of Swaggo Annotations
chapters.description: A look at a sample endpoint demonstrates how to use Swaggo annotations to define endpoint details like summary, parameters, responses, and routing.

chapters.title: Reviewing the Refactored Go API
chapters.description: This section explains the refactored project structure of the sample Fiber API before integrating Swagger documentation.

chapters.title: Installing Dependencies and Initializing Swaggo
chapters.description: This chapter covers installing the Swaggo CLI, running `swag init` to generate the initial docs, and installing the Fiber-Swagger middleware.

chapters.title: Adding Main API Info and First Test
chapters.description: Learn how to add top-level API information using annotations in the main function and understand the workflow of running `swag init` to see changes.

chapters.title: Documenting the GET Order Endpoint
chapters.description: This part details how to write annotations for a GET endpoint, including summary, tags, path parameters, header parameters, and the success response.

chapters.title: Documenting the POST Create Order Endpoint
chapters.description: Learn how to document a POST endpoint, specifying a request body with a custom model, a required header, and both success and failure responses.

chapters.title: Documenting Model Structs and Final Recap
chapters.description: This final chapter shows how to add descriptive comments to struct fields to enrich the model schema in Swagger and provides a summary of the integration process.

summary:
## Core Concept: Declarative API Documentation

Swaggo generates rich, interactive Swagger/OpenAPI documentation by parsing annotations written directly in your Go source code. This approach keeps your API documentation in sync with the code it describes.

## Getting Started with Swaggo

1.  **Install the Swaggo CLI:**
    ```shell
    go install github.com/swaggo/swag/cmd/swag@latest
    ```

2.  **Install the Framework-Specific Wrapper:** For Fiber, you need `fiber-swagger`.
    ```shell
    go get github.com/swaggo/fiber-swagger
    ```

3.  **Generate Documentation:** The `swag init` command parses your annotations and creates a `docs` directory containing the necessary `swagger.json`, `swagger.yaml`, and `docs.go` files.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> You must run `swag init` every time you add or modify annotations to regenerate the documentation files. Otherwise, your changes will not appear in the UI.

## Configuration and Setup

-   **Main API Information:** Add a comment block with annotations above your `main()` function to define global details like the API title, description, and version.

-   **Register the Handler:** Expose the Swagger UI by registering the handler with your Fiber application.
    ```go
    import fiberSwagger "github.com/swaggo/fiber-swagger"
    // ...
    app.Get("/swagger/*", fiberSwagger.WrapHandler)
    ```

## Documenting Endpoints and Models

Use annotation blocks above each handler function to define its behavior.

-   **Key Endpoint Annotations**:
    -   `@Summary`: A short, one-line description.
    -   `@Description`: A more detailed explanation of the endpoint.
    -   `@Tags`: A comma-separated list to group related endpoints (e.g., `Orders`).
    -   `@Router`: Defines the URL path and HTTP method (e.g., `@Router /orders/{code} [get]`).
    -   `@Param`: Describes a single parameter.
        -   **Syntax**: `@Param {name} {location} {type} {required} "Description"`
        -   **`location`**: Can be `path`, `header`, `query`, or `body`.
    -   `@Success`: Describes a successful response (`@Success 200 {object} string`).
    -   `@Failure`: Describes a potential error response (`@Failure 400 {object} string`).

-   **Documenting Models**:
    -   To add descriptions for the fields within a request or response `struct`, simply add a standard Go comment directly above each field.

> [!TIP]
> Use `swag fmt` to automatically format your Swaggo annotations for better consistency and readability.
